seoTitle: How to Merge Indicators in TradingView Into One Pane
metaDescription: Learn how to merge multiple indicators into one pane in TradingView, overlay them on price, and adjust scale settings for cleaner analysis.
intro: Combining indicators into a single pane can make comparisons easier and free up vertical chart space, but it takes a bit of drag-and-drop know-how to get right. This guide walks through merging two indicators into one pane, overlaying them on the main price chart, and adjusting scale settings so everything stays readable. It's aimed at TradingView beginners and strategy builders working with multiple indicators.

steps.heading: Add multiple indicators
steps.body: Apply the indicators you want to combine onto your chart as a starting point.

steps.heading: Merge indicators into one pane
steps.body: Drag one indicator's label into the pane of another to combine them into a single shared panel.

steps.heading: Overlay indicators on the main chart
steps.body: For indicators that support it, drag them onto the main price chart to overlay them directly with candles instead of a separate pane.

steps.heading: Adjust scale settings
steps.body: Fine-tune the scale for merged indicators so their values remain readable and don't overlap awkwardly.

steps.heading: Avoid common mistakes while combining indicators
steps.body: Be mindful of merging indicators with very different value ranges, since this can distort the visual scale and make one indicator hard to read.

faq.question: Can I merge any two indicators into the same pane?
faq.answer: Most indicators can be merged, but combining ones with very different value ranges can make the resulting pane harder to read clearly.

faq.question: How do I move an indicator to the main price chart?
faq.answer: Drag the indicator's label from its current pane directly onto the main price chart if the indicator supports being overlaid.

faq.question: Does merging indicators change how they're calculated?
faq.answer: No, merging only changes the visual placement of indicators on your chart and doesn't affect their underlying calculations.

faq.question: Why would I want to merge indicators like RSI and MACD?
faq.answer: Merging can save vertical chart space and make it easier to compare related indicators side by side, though it's mostly a matter of personal workflow preference.
